pull_requests.title: fix(toolkit): return errors instead of panicking in single-tx and fetcher
pull_requests.description:
# Overview

During Antithesis fault-injection runs (shielded QA), `midnight-node-toolkit` failed the 'No Rust Panics' property with three distinct panics (#1821):

1. `single_tx.rs:161` — `panic!` when the source wallet has insufficient unshielded UTXOs
2. `single_tx.rs:143` — `.expect()` when the source wallet has insufficient shielded coins
3. `fetcher.rs:358` — `attempt to subtract with overflow` in the `fetch_from_rpc` summary log when the queried node's finalized height is below the cached minimum (debug builds only)
4. `fetcher.rs:165` — same underflow in the job-sizing arithmetic, hit in a follow-up validation run when the queried node lagged the cache watermark by more than one block (the line-358 case only covered a lag of exactly one)

Insufficient funds is an expected runtime condition for a CLI, not a programming error. `SingleTxBuilder` now uses a `SingleTxError` thiserror enum (mirroring the existing `BatchSingleTxError` pattern) instead of `type Error = Infallible`: shielded/unshielded coin-selection failures propagate via `#[from]`, proving failures map to `ProvingFailed`, and the empty-transaction case returns `EmptyTransaction`. Errors reach the CLI as a message + non-zero exit through the existing `DynamicError` wrapper. Since the file lives in `builders/common/`, the fix covers the v7/v8/v9 builder instantiations.

All height-span arithmetic in `fetch_from_rpc` (job sizing, receive-loop job count, progress log, summary log) now computes the span once via `saturating_sub`; a zero span degrades to the existing 0-jobs path, which serves blocks from cache.

- `cargo test -p midnight-node-toolkit --lib`: 109 passed, 0 failed (includes `test_generation::single_tx` and `test_batch_single_tx`)

pull_requests.title: feat(local-env): add dedicated `local` network + seed Cardano cNIGHT at genesis
pull_requests.description:
# Overview

Adds a first-class **`local`** network for the dockerized local-environment (its own ledger identity, addresses `mn_addr_local1…`), decoupled from `res/dev`, and **seeds the Cardano side of the cNIGHT↔NIGHT bridge at genesis** so the cross-chain pool invariants hold (fixes #1778).

Why: the local-env previously reused the `undeployed` identity and pulled config from three places (`res/dev`, `res/local-environment`, `res/genesis/*undeployed*`), and the Cardano side minted **0 cNIGHT** at genesis while the Midnight side carried the full NIGHT pools — violating `M.U ≤ C.L` from genesis and leaving the bridge nothing consistent to observe.

**`local` network (#1792):**
- `res/cfg/local.toml` preset + `res/local/` config namespace; `LocalNetwork` registered in `res/src/networks/definitions.rs` (`--chain local` resolves to it; `dev` still maps to `UndeployedNetwork`). `res/local-environment/` retired.
- Unfunded genesis `res/genesis/genesis_{state,block}_local.mn` (Earthfile `rebuild-genesis-state-local`, `FUND_FAUCET_WALLETS=false`); `res/local` ics/reserve totals set so the ledger-state pools `M.R/M.U/M.L` mirror the seeded Cardano amounts.
- `midnight-setup` entrypoint sources all chain-spec config from `res/local/`.

**cNIGHT genesis seeding (#1778):**
- `contract-compiler` exports the deployed `ICS Forever`/`Reserve Forever` addresses + compiled cNIGHT policy; a new `cnight-seeder` service (ordering `contract-compiler → cnight-seeder → midnight-setup`) mints `24e15` cNIGHT and distributes it to mirror the pools — Reserve `C.R=M.R`, ICS `C.L=M.U` (inline unit datum, **no** bridge metadata), faucet `C.U=M.L`.
- `midnight-setup` builds the bridge ICS/Reserve config from the **deployed** validator addresses and anchors `initial_data_checkpoint` to the seeding tx, so the seeded ICS supply is treated as pre-existing locked supply (not swept to Treasury).

## 🗹 TODO before merging

- [ ] Ready
- Note: no node version bump (local-env tooling / additive test network — bump if reviewers prefer).
- Note: `tests/e2e` funding-dependent contract-tx tests are `#[ignore]`d (carry follow-up TODO refs); per-wallet funding is the e2e suite's job (spend the seeded faucet) and is out of scope here.

## 📌 Submission Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) for the DCO
- [x] Changes are backward-compatible (or flagged if breaking)
- [x] Pull request description explains why the change is needed
- [ ] Self-reviewed the diff
- [x] I have included a change file, or skipped for this reason:
- [ ] If the changes introduce a new feature, I have bumped the node minor version <!-- local-env tooling, no runtime change -->
- [ ] Update documentation (if relevant) <!-- covered by the change file -->
- [ ] Updated AGENTS.md if build commands, architecture, or workflows changed <!-- new `rebuild-genesis-state-local` fits the documented `rebuild-genesis-state-<NETWORK>` pattern -->
- [ ] No new todos introduced <!-- deferred e2e tests carry TODO refs -->

## 🧪 Testing Evidence

Verified on a full `npm run run:local-env` run (node image `2.0.0-rc.3`):

- **Cardano side (on-chain):** total `24,000,000,000,000,000` cNIGHT under policy `d2dbff…`; ICS Forever `2,200,000,000,000,000`, Reserve Forever `5,000,000,000,873,988`, faucet `16,799,999,999,126,012`.
- **Midnight side (`toolkit show-night-pools`):** reserve `5,000,000,000,873,988` / unlocked(treasury) `2,200,000,000,000,000` / locked `16,799,999,999,126,012`; TOTAL 24B.
- **M.\* == C.\*** — genesis quiescence holds; `M.U ≤ C.L` satisfied with equality.
- midnight-setup anchored `initial_data_checkpoint` to the seed tx; **no** startup `UnapprovedTransfer`/`UnlockToTreasury` (seeded ICS treated as pre-existing).
- Nodes boot on `local1`, load the unfunded genesis, and finalize blocks (4 peers).

- [ ] Additional tests are provided (if possible) <!-- manual local-env verification above; e2e contract-tx tests deferred -->

- [ ] Node Client Update
- [ ] Other:
- [x] N/A <!-- local-env tooling + an additive test network; no impact on existing networks -->

pull_requests.title: fix(node): backport #1767 to release/node-2.0.0 (accept --no-hardware-benchmarks & --rpc-max-finality-subscriptions)
pull_requests.description:
# Overview

Backports #1767 (merged to `main` as `88eafaff`) to `release/node-2.0.0`.

The fix repairs node startup argument parsing so the custom `RunMidnight` wrapper
flags are accepted. Previously `into_run_cmd()` stripped only `--filter-deploy-txs`
before re-parsing argv with `sc_cli::RunCmd`, so the other two custom flags leaked
through and `RunCmd::parse_from` aborted the process before the node could start:

- `--no-hardware-benchmarks`
- `--rpc-max-finality-subscriptions <value>`

The fix parses `RunMidnight` first, then applies the config overrides to the already
parsed `run_midnight.run` via the new `apply_overrides_to_run_cmd()`.

This is the QA blocker reported on #1395 (the `--no-hardware-benchmarks` disable flag
is an acceptance criterion of that issue). Without this backport, `node-2.0.0-rc.3`
cut from this release branch would still ship the bug.

This is a pure cherry-pick of `88eafaff` (`-x` traceability line included); no code
was modified for the backport.

## 🗹 TODO before merging

- [x] Ready

## 📌 Submission Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) for the DCO
- [x] Changes are backward-compatible (or flagged if breaking)
- [x] Pull request description explains why the change is needed
- [ ] Self-reviewed the diff
- [x] I have included a change file, or skipped for this reason: pure cherry-pick of #1767, which carried no change file; `skip-changes-check-all` applied
- [ ] If the changes introduce a new feature, I have bumped the node minor version
- [ ] Update documentation (if relevant)
- [ ] Updated AGENTS.md if build commands, architecture, or workflows changed
- [x] No new todos introduced

## 🧪 Testing Evidence

Retested on `release/node-2.0.0` with the cherry-pick applied, release build (`cargo build --release`).

**Baseline (pre-fix binary)** — both flags abort at arg parsing with exit 2:
```
$ midnight-node --no-hardware-benchmarks --tmp --dev --no-prometheus
error: unexpected argument '--no-hardware-benchmarks' found
$ midnight-node --rpc-max-finality-subscriptions 256 --tmp --dev --no-prometheus
error: unexpected argument '--rpc-max-finality-subscriptions' found
```

**With fix** — node boots past arg parsing and produces blocks in all cases:

| Test | `unexpected argument`? | Boots & produces blocks? | Benchmark runs? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-hardware-benchmarks` | No | Yes (consensus + block #1) | No (0 lines) — flag suppresses it |
| `--rpc-max-finality-subscriptions 256` | No | Yes (best #4 / finalized #1) | Yes (expected) |
| control (plain `--dev`) | No | Yes (best #3 / finalized #1) | Yes (expected) |

`--no-hardware-benchmarks` was also confirmed functional, not merely accepted: 0 benchmark
log lines vs 4 in the control run.

- [ ] Additional tests are provided (if possible)

## 🔱 Fork Strategy

- [x] Node Client Update

Related issue (QA blocker): https://github.com/midnightntwrk/midnight-node/issues/1395
Original PR: https://github.com/midnightntwrk/midnight-node/pull/1767

issues.title: Run the standard Substrate hardware benchmark checks automatically when `midnight-node` starts
issues.description:
## Describe the proposed feature
Run the standard Substrate hardware benchmark checks automatically when `midnight-node` starts.
The node should:
- gather CPU, memory, and disk benchmark data on startup
- print the benchmark results to the logs
- warn when an authority node does not meet the reference hardware requirements
- forward the benchmark data to telemetry when telemetry is enabled
- support `--no-hardware-benchmarks` to disable the startup check
## User Need
Operators need early visibility into whether the machine running `midnight-node` is suitable for validator/authority workloads.
Without this startup check, a node can start normally on underpowered hardware and only reveal performance issues later through degraded behavior. Matching the standard Polkadot SDK startup behavior makes the node more predictable for operators and easier to assess during deployment.
## Expected Benefit
This improves operator feedback at startup, aligns `midnight-node` behavior with upstream Substrate/Polkadot SDK nodes, and helps prevent misconfigured or underpowered authority deployments.
It also exposes the benchmark data through telemetry, which makes it easier to reason about node environments remotely.
## Details
Implementation should follow the existing Polkadot SDK startup flow:
- collect `hwbench` before starting the full node
- pass the collected benchmark data into node startup/service initialization
- print benchmark results during startup
- check them against `SUBSTRATE_REFERENCE_HARDWARE`
- warn for authority nodes that do not meet the minimum requirements
- initialize hardware benchmark telemetry when telemetry is enabled
